To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complete fusion excitation function in the 6Li + 144Sm reaction is suppressed by 32% and the suppression factor is a function of the atomic numbers of the target nucleus and the breakup threshold of projectile.
complete fusion cross sections are systematically lower than the predictions of the one-dimensional barrier-penetration model in reactions with weakly bound projectiles and strongly bound targets.
fusion suppression factors for the 6,7 Li projectiles, which form a similar compound nucleus, are significantly different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the complete fusion cross sections for 6 Li + Sm-144 and 7 Li+ Ho-165 and 159 Tb.
the study of the suppression of the complete fusion in heavy ion reactions at near barrier energies, which has been a topic of great interest for the past few years.
a systematic study of the complete fusion cross sections in the 6,7 Li + Sm reactions at near barrier energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the complete fusion is suppressed in the 6,7 Li + 144,159,165 Sm systems compared to the fusion cross sections with strongly bound projectiles.
the complete fusion is suppressed in the reactions involving loosely bound projectiles, which is attributed to the breakup of the projectiles in the entrance channel.
the fusion suppression factor for the 6,7 Li projectiles is ∼32% and it increases with increasing projectile breakup threshold and target atomic number.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the suppression of complete fusion in 6 Li induced reactions is not due to the breakup of 6 Li projectile at near barrier energies.
the fusion suppression in the Li-7 + Ho-165 and the Li-7+Tb-159 reactions is about 30% and the suppression in the Li 6 + Sm- 144 reaction is ∼32% at above barrier energies.
the complete fusion is suppressed in the Li + medium mass target reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fusion suppression is a general phenomenon, not just a property of weakly bound projectiles, as was earlier thought.
the fusion suppression factor, at energies normalized to their respective Coulomb barriers, is a function of the projectile breakup threshold and atomic number of the compound nucleus.
the suppression in fusion cross section is not due to the projectile breakup, but it is a general feature of the 6 Li-induced reactions.
